It is obtained by the metric outer-measure construction mkMetric with gauge r↦r^a on extended nonnegative diameters: at each positive scale take the maximal outer measure bounded by the gauge on all nonempty sets of at most that diameter, then take the supremum over scales and its Borel-measure realization. Values on arbitrary sets mean outer-measure values. Empty covering members cost zero and nonempty members cost diam^a with extended nonnegative-real powers; at a=0 a nonempty singleton has cost 1.

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of subsets of metric spaces, valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition: dimH(A), also written dim_H A, is the standard Hausdorff dimension: sup({a≥0 : muH(a)(A)=infinity}) in [0,infinity], where the supremum of an empty set is 0. This is the native dimH definition. The notation uses the empty-set dimension convention 0. Critical-exponent properties and agreement with the supplied positive-exponent diameter-cost measure are proof obligations, not extra assumptions.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.type: subset of R
Lebesgue measure on R and associated integral notation
definitions.definition: lambda is the standard Lebesgue measure on R with its Borel measurable structure and the normalization by interval length. For a Borel set J, |J| denotes lambda(J). The symbol 1_J denotes its indicator, equal to 1 on J and 0 elsewhere. Integrals of nonnegative functions are extended Lebesgue integrals (native lintegral). Restriction to I is lambda restricted to [0,1]. The usual interval values are lambda(I)=1 and lambda((a,b))=b-a for a<b; only these interval values are used.

inputs.statement: For every nonnegative integer k, every A⊆Eucl(k), and every real a>0, H^a(A)=muH(a)(A). Consequently: a>dimH(A) implies H^a(A)=0; 0<a<dimH(A) implies H^a(A)=infinity; H^a(A)=0 implies dimH(A)≤a; and H^a(A)=infinity implies dimH(A)≥a. Hausdorff dimension is nonnegative. For A⊆B⊆Eucl(k), dimH(A)≤dimH(B). For every nonnegative integer l and every distance-preserving map g:A→Eucl(l), dimH(g(A))=dimH(A).

For every type X, every type G of set-functions from subsets of X to [0,infinity] equipped with a function-like outer-measure-class structure, every outer-measure-class element nu in G, every countable type T and every family W:T→subsets of X, nu(union_{i in T} W(i)) ≤ sum_{i in T} nu(W(i)). No measurability assumption on W(i) is needed.

binders.type: function-like type of functions from subsets of X to [0,infinity], with outer-measure-class structure

source_conditions: G has the stated function-like outer-measure-class structure on X and nu belongs to G.
T is countable.

locals.declaration: Fix a>1 for the interval upper estimate.
For the lower estimate fix any 0<s<1.
Fix any delta>0.

locals.type: countable family of subsets of R
locals.declaration: Let V be a countable family, temporarily assumed in L1 to be a delta-cover of I.
After enumeration and empty padding, T is the set of nonempty-member indices of V.

locals.type: T-indexed family of nonnegative real numbers
locals.declaration: Set rho_i=diam(V_i) for i in T.
Fix arbitrary epsilon>0.

locals.type: T-indexed family of open bounded intervals
locals.declaration: For i in T set J_i=(inf V_i-epsilon 2^(-i-2),sup V_i+epsilon 2^(-i-2)); each V_i is nonempty with finite diameter by L1.

argument.text: For any a>1, the N equal closed subintervals of I, with N a positive integer, have diameter 1/N and total a-cost N^(1-a) tending to zero, while their mesh tends to zero. At each fixed scale they are eventually admissible with arbitrarily small cost, so H^a(I)=0. By N001, dimH(I)≤a for every a>1 and hence dimH(I)≤1.

produces.statement: dimH(I)≤1.

argument.text: For the lower estimate fix 0<s<1 and delta>0. Let V be any countable family and introduce L1: it is a delta-cover of I. Enumerate with empty padding and let T⊆N index the nonempty members. Put rho_i=diam(V_i)≤delta. Each V_i is a bounded nonempty subset of R, so sup V_i-inf V_i=rho_i. For any epsilon>0 define J_i=(inf V_i-epsilon 2^(-i-2),sup V_i+epsilon 2^(-i-2)). These open intervals contain V_i and have length rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1). Thus they cover I and are Borel measurable.

produces.statement: I⊆union_{i in T}J_i, and each J_i is an open bounded interval of length rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1).

argument.text: Apply M005 to Lebesgue measure lambda, the countable index type T, and the intervals J_i. Measure monotonicity and F002 yield 1=lambda(I)≤lambda(union_i J_i)≤sum_i lambda(J_i)=sum_i(rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1))≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon. If sum_i rho_i is infinite then sum_i rho_i≥1 already; otherwise let epsilon decrease to zero. The V,rho and T do not depend on epsilon, so sum_i rho_i≥1 in all cases.

produces.statement: sum_{i in T}rho_i≥1.

argument.text: Because 0<s<1 and 0≤rho_i≤delta, rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)rho_i: for rho_i>0 divide by rho_i and use the decreasing power with negative exponent s-1; for rho_i=0 both sides are zero. Hence sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1) by F003. Discharge L1 and take the infimum over all delta-covers V. This proves H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1) for every delta>0.

produces.statement: For every d0>0, H^s_d0(I)≥d0^(s-1).

argument.text: Since s-1<0, delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, and F004 implies H^s(I)=infinity. By N001, dimH(I)≥s for every s∈(0,1). Letting s increase to 1 gives dimH(I)≥1. Combining with F001 proves dimH(I)=1, with no missing zero-dimensional ambient case.

applications.bindings: Source X=R; G is the type of measures on R, with its usual function-like outer-measure-class structure; nu=lambda; countable source index type=T⊆N; W(i)=J_i.
hypothesis_checks: Lebesgue measure lambda is a measure by D009; measures carry their standard function-like outer-measure-class structure.
T is a subset of N by S002, hence countable.

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
